title: Introduce model_history.log and deterministic delta-apply hook for profile changelogs
author: Lena Park
release_notes: Adds persistent model_history.log to record onboarding deltas
Adds delta-apply CLI hook to generate deterministic changelogs for model profile updates
Includes a backwards-compatible migration script to convert legacy profile diffs into the new history format
Improves release-note fidelity and reduces changelog generation latency for large registries
description:
Motivation: generating release notes for model profile updates has become slow and noisy as we scale the registry. Small consecutive edits to metadata and perf profiles produced fragmented changelogs and made rollouts confusing. This PR introduces a compact, append-only model_history.log and a deterministic 'delta-apply' hook that normalizes incoming profile diffs into semantic changelog entries.

What this PR changes: model_history.log: a per-model append-only JSONL artifact schema (registry/model_history.log.schema.yaml) that records normalized deltas with fields: version, timestamp, actor, change_kind, profile_hash, diff_summary, and tags. The file is intentionally metadata-only (no prompt or raw input) to preserve privacy.

delta-apply CLI hook: cli/delta_apply.py implements the deterministic consolidation algorithm. The hook consumes a sequence of raw profile diffs, applies normalization (field ordering, numeric bucketing, name canonicalization) and produces a stable set of changelog entries used by the release notes generator. This eliminates churn from semantically-equivalent edits (e.g., whitespace, float precision).

Migration: migrations/2024_11_migrate_legacy_profiles.py converts legacy profile-diff artifacts into model_history.log entries. The migration is idempotent and emits a migration report stored under migrations/reports/*. The migration is safe to run on existing registries and has a dry-run flag.

Tooling and docs: added templates/changelog-template.mustache and scripts/generate-release-notes.sh to demonstrate deterministic generation of release notes across CI and the Console. Documentation in docs/registry/release-notes.md explains the workflow for engineers and product.

Backward compatibility and safety: existing profile files and the onboarding pipeline continue to work. The delta-apply hook can be inserted as an optional step during onboarding; we ship the migration to bootstrap history logs for prior models. model_history.log intentionally stores high-level diffs only and omits any PII or prompt contents.

Performance: in internal tests with a synthetic registry of 12k models and 85k profile edits, changelog assembly time fell from ~18s to ~1.3s (wall-clock) and peak memory usage dropped by ~65%.

Testing: added tests/test_delta_apply.py that covers normalization rules, hash stability, and idempotence. CI pipeline additions ensure migration dry-run passes on a snapshot dataset.

Follow-ups: (a) expose a Console view for model_history.log entries and search by tag (ENG-3492), (b) wire the delta-apply output to Redwood Optimize quality regressions (ENG-3510), (c) add rate-limited history compaction for extremely chatty models (future PR).

Related: ties to ENG-3489 (release-note quality), PM-712 (product spec for changelog UX), and SUP-1982 (customer case showing confusing changelogs).
